reading.body:
CyrusOne Lewisville DFW2 publishes 12 MW of IT capacity, enough for roughly 80 racks of AI accelerator infrastructure at 150 kW per rack, but below the 50+ MW threshold for current large-scale AI training clusters.

The facility holds six compliance certifications spanning healthcare, finance, government, and security sectors. This regulatory posture matters for regulated AI workloads, though the data does not indicate whether the facility currently hosts such applications or has infrastructure optimized for them.

Lewisville DFW2 represents 2.5 percent of Texas's published 475 MW of data center capacity. Texas has 133 mapped data center sites, but only 19 publish power figures. This opacity makes it impossible to know whether the state's true capacity is substantially larger, or whether most facilities are individually small.

The facility's 12 MW places it below current AI infrastructure requirements. AI training clusters now typically span 50+ MW per campus. A single facility of this size could support inference workloads or smaller training runs, but not the scale of compute buildouts now driving power demand in major AI hubs.
